title: "Aquatic Sediment"

Working document for the **Aquatic Sediment** grouping: 16 groups, 27,306 measurements.

Scaffolded 2026-08-04 by `scripts/generate_group_notebooks.R`. **The generator is append-only**: re-running it adds sections for new groups and never touches anything already written here, so this file is yours to edit freely.

Figures and counts are static, written at scaffold time rather than computed on render. Group ids are stable (`data/clean/decisions/group_ids.csv`), so they remain the reliable way to refer back to a group even if the numbers here go stale.

# Overview

**Overview, `mg/kg (dry)`.** `n` = 27,288 measurements in 13 groups below this sub-compartment.

@fig-aquatic-aquatic-sediment-mg-kg-dry shows roughly log-normal distributions for most *Site Geographical Feature* types. Most data (n = 25,024, 2 sources) were sampled from *Coastal/fjord Water benthos*, and are clustered around a mean of 94.1 and geometric mean of 20.6 mg/kg (dry weight). Concentrations for this group vary by 9 orders of magnitude from as little as 1e-03 to as much as 1e05.5 mg/kg.

Variation in other *Site Geographical Feature* types covers a substantially smaller range of values (roughly 1e+03.5 to 1e-03). A not insubstantial portion of sampled concentrations exceed the highest M-608 threshold (IV:

TODO: THe highest threshold is V, according to comments. Why isn't it here?

> **Answered and fixed 2026-08-05.** `THRESHOLD_VALUE` in the source data is the **upper** boundary of the class it names, and the lines were labelled that way, so every line read one class low and Class V could never appear: its own upper boundary is open-ended and there is no line to draw at infinity.
>
> Lines are now named for the class they **open**, which is also the reading you asked for ("we're interested in knowing when concentrations exceed it"). The sediment ladder now labels 20 / 84 / 147 as **II / IV / V**. Class I loses its line, its lower bound being zero. Colour and linetype shifted with the labels, so the topmost line is now Very Poor red and solid rather than Poor orange.
>
> Coastal water needed a data fix to go with it: it had no Class V row at all, so its 5.2 μg/L line had nothing to take a name from. Added as an open-ended row, matching freshwater and sediment.

- Some sediment also sampled from column - seems to have a slightly lower mean than benthos (which seems reasonable)

# Comparison

::: {.callout-note}
Gut feeling - aquatic sediment will be a mixture of 1e3 errors and campaigns. Sediment from different site times probably are slightly different, because biogeochemistry, hydrology, etc. will be different, but this might not be a strong enough signal. We also have some very small sample sizes. My initial reaction is that we should drop any samples that correspond to suspended sediment (e.g. *Water column, pelagic zone* rather than *Water benthos*), because they're a small proportion of the overall group and they require a level of resolution that I don't think we can consistently provide with the data we have.
:::

# Groups

## G002-Wsd-Cwb-Md Aquatic / Aquatic Sediment / Coastal, fjord / Water benthos / mg/kg (dry) {#grp-G002-Wsd-Cwb-Md}

`G002-Wsd-Cwb-Md` `n` = 25,024 measurements, from **2** sources (distinct `REFERENCE_ID`). Unit: `mg/kg (dry)`.

::: callout-warning
## Flagged

- **multimodal** (dip test not run)
:::

Distribution here (\@fig-g002-wsd-cwb-md-a) is normal-ish and centered slightly above the background concentration, but there's clearly at least one sub-peak at \~1e+00.5. Large right tail, and many samples at extremely high concentrations, which suggests unit errors. @fig-g002-wsd-cwb-md-b shows no clear temporal pattern, but central tendency around the aquatic sediment background (I) threshold from 2016 onwards. A few big outliers in specific years are perhaps errors rather than true variation. @fig-g002-wsd-cwb-md-c shows that with a handful of exceptions, campaigns have similar medians, but different patterns of outliers. @coteurFieldContaminationStarfish2003's concentrations have a median around 1e-03 and are several orders of magnitude lower than those from @norwegianenvironmentagencyVannmiljo2026. Some campaigns have slightly higher medians (Urban Fjord Contaminants), while Screening New Contaminants has a surprisingly low median with a lot of spread (but small sample size). No campaigns are explicitly and only focused on non-contaminated sites (e.g. Reference sites), so it is difficult to determine if there's a real difference between contaminated and uncontaminated sites. Probably inconclusive without looking at sampling depth, more detailed site information, and fractionation. @fig-g002-wsd-cwb-md-d mainly shows site coding atefacts, in any case, there seems to be no substantial difference between settled and suspended sediment. @fig-g002-wsd-cwb-md-e shows that most areas (at the current resolution) fall between 1e01 and 1e04, which isn't enough concentration resolution.

TODO: Have I made a unit error with Coteur

> **CONFIRMED against the paper, 2026-08-05: Coteur reports μg g⁻¹ dry weight, and the source file records μg/kg (dry). Still to fix in `data/raw/eData/`.**
>
> Chasing it turned up a **second and larger fault in the pipeline**, which was silently dividing every genuine `μg/g` row by 1000: 93 rows across 11 other references, all now corrected. It also recovered 18 rows of Julshamn seal data whose micro sign had been destroyed by an encoding round-trip. See PLAN.md section 9b.
>
> The original evidence follows.
>
> **Note to self, checked 2026-08-05. Almost certainly yes, and it looks like μg/g read as μg/kg.**
>
> All 28 Coteur rows are stored as `μg/kg (dry)` and standardised by ×1e-3. Against every other source in the same compartment and unit:
>
> |   | Coteur geo. mean | Others geo. mean | Ratio |
> |----|---:|---:|---:|
> | Aquatic Sediment, mg/kg (dry) | 0.034 | 21.3 | 619× (2.79 orders) |
> | Biota, Aquatic, mg/kg (dry) | 0.012 | 2.80 | 229× (2.36 orders) |
>
> The raw numbers as entered are 8 to 100 for sediment and 2.7 to 92 for *A. rubens* tissue. Read as **mg/kg** those are entirely ordinary values for both matrices; read as μg/kg they are implausible, since 0.03 mg/kg dry sediment is below crustal abundance. **μg/g = mg/kg**, so a source reporting μg/g transcribed as μg/kg gives exactly this 1000× error. The observed ratios are 619× and 229× rather than 1000× only because the comparison is against a different population of sites, not the same samples.
>
> Fix belongs in the extraction, not the pipeline. Until then Coteur will keep appearing as the lowest campaign on every sediment and echinoderm panel.

The key is now one bin per order of magnitude with the M-608 boundaries inserted and named, instead of ggplot2 choosing 6 breaks over 12.6 orders. Thresholds cannot be drawn as lines on this panel: its axes are lon/lat and concentration is the fill, so a threshold has no position in the panel. **The remaining resolution problem is the shared scale, and it is your call** — see the note below.)*

> **Why fig-e still looks flat, measured 2026-08-05. Three separate causes, and the biggest one is the data, not the plot.**
>
> The colour scale spans the whole `Aquatic` compartment, which is 12.3 orders of magnitude, so a sediment group occupying 3 of them uses a quarter of the palette however many bins there are.
>
> | Change                              |               Aquatic span |
> |-------------------------------------|---------------------------:|
> | now (limits per compartment)        |                12.3 orders |
> | limits per compartment **and unit** | 8.3 orders for mg/kg (dry) |
> | 1st to 99th percentile of that      |             **2.8 orders** |
>
> So splitting the limits by unit buys 4 orders and is a one-line change to `compute_triage_scale_limits(by = ...)`. **It costs the property P1.1d was built for**: dry and wet weight would no longer share an axis, so panel (a), whose entire purpose is comparing them, would need its own limits.
>
> The larger finding is the third row. **99% of sediment rows sit within 2.8 orders**; the full 8.3 comes from about 1% at the two tails. The bottom is the Coteur unit error noted above (0.0013 mg/kg dry) and the top is the 270,000 mg/kg dry value flagged in PLAN.md P1.1d, which is 27% copper by mass, i.e. ore rather than sediment. Fixing those two does more for the resolution of this panel than any scale change.
>
> Three options, in the order I would take them: (1) chase the two tails, since they are data errors that will distort means and thresholds too; (2) split the limits by unit and give panel (a) its own; (3) clip the colour scale to a percentile range and mark out-of-range cells. Not doing any of them unilaterally because all three change a figure the manuscript may use.

- @fig-g008-wsd-rwb-md-a: at least two log-normal distributions with slightly different means (one below I, one above), plus characteristic 1e3 unit error slopes.

- @fig-g008-wsd-rwb-md-b: no obvious time trend. highest concentration of samples in 2017, doesn't look log-normal but may be resolution artifact. some outlier noise apparent.

- @fig-g008-wsd-rwb-md-d: as with other sediment sampling groups, suspended sediment concentrations appear to generally be higher than those taken from benthos (though this may be artefact of methodology). given the much wider spread of benthic samples, these could probably be lumped.
